messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: hosted-gpu-pool-3 capacity threshold breached (94%). Queue growth detected on /v1/generate. p95 latency > 3s, p99 > 12s. Automated scale attempted but failed (quota error). Paging sasha_oncall :rotating_light:

incident-bot: recent events: 
- 2107778970: sudden request spike from customer 'atlas-ml' (~4x baseline)
- 2107779000: autoscaler attempt -> API 403: quota.limit.exceeded
- 2107779010: queue length increased from 120 -> 860 requests

sasha_oncall: I'm on it. I see the 403 in the autoscaler logs. Will check quota and pool state.

miguel_sre: heads-up, I just saw hosted-gpu-pool-3 report OOM on a few nodes earlier (maybe a failing upgrade). Could be causing the autoscaler to not count nodes as healthy.

sasha_oncall: good call. Running quick health: `curl -s http://infra-api.local/pools/pool-3/health | jq .` -> lots of `failed=true` entries.

laura_prod: customer impact: Support reported increased timeouts for Atlas infra integration. CS ticket #CS-4821 created by eve_support. Atlas getting 503s and retries.

nithya_re: If pool nodes are flapping health checks, autoscaler will think capacity is still low and keep trying to add but API returns quota. We need two parallel mitigations: 1) open temporary fallback routing to pool-1 (less loaded) and 2) throttle heavy customers to protect general traffic.

ben_ops: I'll open a bridge in 5m unless you want one now.

sasha_oncall: open bridge now pls. /bridge ops-incident (started)

ben_ops: bridge up -> https://bridge.redwood/ops/2107779012 (DM for link) :white_check_mark:

miguel_sre: quick mitigation plan:
- 1) add emergency routing rule to route non-SLA traffic to pool-1 (safer).
- 2) temporarily reduce per-customer concurrency for top 10 callers to 1/2.
- 3) scale up pool-3 manually if quota can be increased by infra team.
- 4) fallback to smaller quantized model variant for non-critical requests.

sasha_oncall: executing 1 & 2 now. Patching routing config:```
PATCH /api/v1/routing/policies/hosted
{ "rules": [{"match":"/v1/generate","action":"route","target":"pool-1","priority":10,"condition":"customer != 'atlas-ml' and customer_tier != 'enterprise'"}]
}
```

sasha_oncall: applied patch, waiting for propagation. Will monitor queue.

incident-bot: routing change propagated to edge nodes (approx 45s). Observability: queue length starting to flatten but still high (460).

laura_prod: notifying CS: "We're rerouting lower-priority traffic to alternate pool and throttling heavy customers. We see degraded latency for Atlas and are working on capacity increase. We'll follow up in 30m."

eve_support: sent note to Atlas PM. They reported retries/backoffs implemented on their side but want ETA.

miguel_sre: For step 3 I can open a support ticket to cloud provider for quota bump, but ETA ~ 20-40m. In parallel, we should try to reclaim any unhealthy nodes in pool-3: `ssh` in and restart inference agent on nodes in failing set.

sasha_oncall: I'm rotating a small manual scale up for pool-3 using reserved GPUs we have in staging -> will move 2 nodes to production. Command: `infra-cli pool attach --pool pool-3 --node-type a100-40g --count 2 --from staging` (manual move)

ben_ops: caution: moving staging nodes will reduce staging capacity by ~30%. QA will be affected. I've notified QA slack.

nithya_re: while you move nodes, enable model-fallback for non-enterprise customers. Patch below:```
PATCH /api/v1/models/serve
{ "fallback": [{"from":"redwood/open-30b","to":"redwood/open-7b-q4_0","condition":"customer_tier != 'enterprise'"}]
}
```

sasha_oncall: applied fallback. Observability shows immediate per-token CPU drop on pool-1/pool-3, throughput per GPU increased.

incident-bot: alert: queue p95 now 1.4s, p99 4.8s. Total queue 210. Autoscaler still returning quota.limit.exceeded on attempts to allocate more hosts.

laura_prod: customer impact summary to execs (draft): "Atlas: experiencing elevated error rates and latency from 12:02 UTC to 12:26 UTC. Partial mitigation applied at 12:14 UTC by routing and throttling; full service restored for most traffic by 12:22 UTC. Enterprise traffic remained on larger models and saw minor latency increases. Root causes being investigated: combination of sudden traffic spike + pool node instability + cloud quota block."

miguel_sre: FYI logs snippet from pool-3 node-17:```
[12:07:21] inference-agent ERROR: worker OOM at step=token_gen
[12:08:03] health-check FAILED: agent-unresponsive
[12:09:12] cloud-api error: quota.limit.exceeded for attach-hosts
```

eve_support: Atlas reported a drop in errors after we told them to retry with exponential backoff and we applied routing. They still want a postmortem and root cause.

sasha_oncall: status update: staging nodes migrated -> pool-3 +2 nodes added manually. Agents restarted on previously failing nodes. Health checks now passing for those nodes.

incident-bot: autoscaler attempts resumed. Next allocation succeeded 12:29 UTC. Queue drained to <50 by 12:34 UTC.

nithya_re: recommended follow-ups for postmortem:
- Confirm why nodes in pool-3 flapped (recent kernel/driver update?).
- Improve autoscaler error handling for quota errors (backoff + alert to infra team).
- Add pre-warm path: if queue > 500 and provider quota prevents scale, auto-enable model-fallback + aggressive throttling rule to protect tail latencies.
- Add rate-limited sticky tokens for heavy customers so they don't spike concurrency.

ben_ops: I'll create incident ticket and schedule blameless postmortem. Assign to miguel, sasha, nithya.

laura_prod: I'm drafting customer-facing timeline. Will include mitigation timeline and ask Atlas if they can share request pattern for debugging.

miguel_sre: allocating follow-up tasks in tracker: INF-1284 (node flaps), INF-1285 (autoscaler quota handling), INF-1286 (routing pre-warm policy).

sasha_oncall: final status: degraded from 12:02 -> 12:22 UTC, major mitigation actions at 12:14 (routing+throttle) and 12:24 (manual node attach). All services healthy at 12:36 UTC.

eve_support: adding customer note to CS ticket and closing the active support alert after Atlas confirms recovery.

laura_prod: thanks team. After postmortem we'll iterate on improved runbooks for on-call and a runbook snippet to enable model-fallback + throttles as fast mitigation. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSE RECOMMENDATION: Queue metrics stable for 20m, no active escalations. Please ack to close.

sasha_oncall: ack. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
